passages.text: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead.
Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany.
Bethany was the hometown of Lazarus.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα ἦλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν ὅπου ἦν Λάζαρος ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.
passages.sermon:
The people in Bethany hosted a dinner for Jesus.
Martha served the meal.
Lazarus was at the table with Jesus.
Lazarus was one of those reclining with Him.
passages.original: ἐποίησαν οὖν αὐτῷ δεῖπνον ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ Μάρθα διηκόνει ὁ δὲ Λάζαρος εἷς ἦν ἐκ τῶν ἀνακειμένων σὺν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
passages.sermon:
Mary was there in Bethany.
Mary took a pint of expensive perfume.
The perfume was made of pure nard.
Mary anointed Jesus’ feet with the perfume.
Mary wiped Jesus’ feet with her hair.
The house became filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
passages.original: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ λαβοῦσα λίτραν μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτίμου ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐξέμαξεν ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ἡ δὲ οἰκία ἐπληρώθη ἐκ τῆς ὀσμῆς τοῦ μύρου

passages.text: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked, “Why wasn’t this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”
passages.sermon:
Judas Iscariot was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Judas Iscariot was going to betray Jesus.
Judas Iscariot spoke.
Judas Iscariot asked a question.
He said, “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii?”
He said, “Why was the money not given to the poor?”
passages.original: Λέγει δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ μέλλων αὐτὸν παραδιδόναι Διὰ τί τοῦτο τὸ μύρον οὐκ ἐπράθη τριακοσίων δηναρίων καὶ ἐδόθη πτωχοῖς

passages.text: Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.
passages.sermon:
Judas Iscariot was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Judas was going to betray Jesus.
Judas did not care about the poor.
Judas was a thief.
Judas kept the money bag.
Judas took money from what was put into the bag.
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ τοῦτο οὐχ ὅτι περὶ τῶν πτωχῶν ἔμελεν αὐτῷ ἀλλ’ ὅτι κλέπτης ἦν καὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον ἔχων τὰ βαλλόμενα ἐβάσταζεν

passages.text: “Leave her alone,” Jesus replied. “She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke.
Jesus said, “Leave her alone.”
She has kept this perfume.
She kept it to prepare for the day of My burial.
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄφες αὐτήν ἵνα εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ ἐνταφιασμοῦ μου τηρήσῃ αὐτό

passages.text: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus said, “You will always have poor people with you.\r\nYou will not always have Me with you.”
passages.original: τοὺς πτωχοὺς γὰρ πάντοτε ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε

passages.text: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
passages.sermon:
A large crowd of Jews heard that Jesus was there.
They came to the place where Jesus was.
They did not come only to see Jesus.
They also wanted to see Lazarus.
Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead.
passages.original: Ἔγνω οὖν ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὅτι ἐκεῖ ἐστιν καὶ ἦλθον οὐ διὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἴδωσιν ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well, for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests made plans.
They wanted to kill Lazarus too.
Many Jews saw Lazarus.
Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead.
Because of Lazarus, many Jews left the chief priests.
These Jews believed in Jesus.
passages.original: ἐβουλεύσαντο δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἀποκτείνωσιν ὅτι πολλοὶ δι’ αὐτὸν ὑπῆγον τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐπίστευον εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: A large crowd of people had come to the feast in Jerusalem.\r\nThe next day, this crowd heard news about Jesus.\r\nThey heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ὁ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
passages.sermon:
A large crowd came to the feast in Jerusalem.
The people heard that Jesus was coming.
They took palm branches in their hands.
They went out to meet Jesus.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “Hosanna!”
They said, “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
They said, “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
passages.original: ἔλαβον τὰ βαΐα τῶν φοινίκων καὶ ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐκραύγαζον Ὡσαννά Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου Καὶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus found a young donkey.
Jesus sat on the young donkey.
Scripture had written about this event.
Scripture says, “Do not be afraid, Daughter of Zion.”
Scripture says, “Look, your King is coming.”
Scripture says, “He is sitting on a young donkey.”
passages.original: Εὑρὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὀνάριον ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτό καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον Μὴ φοβοῦ θυγάτηρ Σιών ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται καθήμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου

passages.text: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
At first, His disciples did not understand these things.
People did things to Jesus.
Scripture had written about these things.
Later, Jesus was glorified.
After this, His disciples remembered what had been done to Him.
They realized that these things had also been written about Him.
passages.original: Ταῦτα οὐκ ἔγνωσαν αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ τὸ πρῶτον ἀλλ’ ὅτε ἐδοξάσθη Ἰησοῦς τότε ἐμνήσθησαν ὅτι ταῦτα ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα καὶ ταῦτα ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Meanwhile, many people continued to testify that they had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.
passages.sermon:
Many people had been with Jesus.
These people saw Jesus call Lazarus from the tomb.
They saw Jesus raise Lazarus from the dead.
These people continued to testify about what they saw.
passages.original: Ἐμαρτύρει οὖν ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ὢν μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὅτε τὸν Λάζαρον ἐφώνησεν ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου καὶ ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had performed a miraculous sign.
The people heard about this sign.
The crowd wanted to see Jesus.
The crowd went out to meet Him because of what they heard.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι ἤκουσαν τοῦτο αὐτὸν πεποιηκέναι τὸ σημεῖον

passages.text: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
\r\nThey spoke to each other.
\r\nThey said, “We are not succeeding.”
\r\nThey said, “Nothing we do is helping.”
\r\nThey said, “Look at this.”
\r\nThey said, “Everyone is following Jesus.”
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν Φαρισαῖοι εἶπαν πρὸς ἑαυτούς Θεωρεῖτε ὅτι οὐκ ὠφελεῖτε οὐδέν ἴδε ὁ κόσμος ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
passages.sermon: Some Greeks were present.\r\nThese Greeks had come to the feast.\r\nThey went up to worship at the feast.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ Ἕλληνές τινες ἐκ τῶν ἀναβαινόντων ἵνα προσκυνήσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ

passages.text: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
passages.sermon:
Some Greeks went to Philip.
Philip came from Bethsaida in Galilee.
The Greeks spoke to Philip.
They said, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
passages.original: οὗτοι οὖν προσῆλθον Φιλίππῳ τῷ ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Κύριε θέλομεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδεῖν

passages.text: Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a disciple of Jesus.
Philip came to Andrew.
Andrew was also a disciple of Jesus.
Philip spoke to Andrew.
Then Andrew and Philip went together.
Andrew and Philip spoke to Jesus.
They told Jesus about the request.
passages.original: ἔρχεται ὁ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἀνδρέᾳ ἔρχεται Ἀνδρέας καὶ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγουσιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus answered their request.
Jesus said, “The time has come.
Now the Son of Man will be glorified.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκρίνεται αὐτοῖς λέγων Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
A kernel of wheat is a single seed.
If the seed does not fall to the ground and die, it stays alone.
If the seed dies in the ground, it produces much fruit.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ ὁ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου πεσὼν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἀποθάνῃ αὐτὸς μόνος μένει ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ πολὺν καρπὸν φέρει

passages.text: Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus said, “Whoever loves his own life will lose it.
Whoever hates his life in this world will keep it.
He will keep it for eternal life.”
passages.original: ὁ φιλῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολλύει αὐτήν καὶ ὁ μισῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον φυλάξει αὐτήν

passages.text: If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
If anyone serves Jesus, that person must follow Jesus.
Where Jesus is, His servant will also be there.
If anyone serves Jesus, the Father will honor that person.
passages.original: ἐὰν ἐμοί τις διακονῇ ἐμοὶ ἀκολουθείτω καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ διάκονος ὁ ἐμὸς ἔσται ἐάν τις ἐμοὶ διακονῇ τιμήσει αὐτὸν ὁ Πατήρ

passages.text: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Himself.
Jesus said His soul felt troubled.
He asked what He should say.
He considered saying, “Father, save Me from this hour.”
But Jesus said He came for this very purpose.
He came to this hour for this reason.
passages.original: Νῦν ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται καὶ τί εἴπω Πάτερ σῶσόν με ἐκ τῆς ὥρας ταύτης ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ὥραν ταύτην

passages.text: Father, glorify Your name!” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to God the Father.
Jesus said, "Father, glorify Your name."
A voice came from heaven.
The voice said, "I have glorified it."
The voice also said, "I will glorify it again."
passages.original: Πάτερ δόξασόν σου τὸ ὄνομα Ἦλθεν οὖν φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Καὶ ἐδόξασα καὶ πάλιν δοξάσω

passages.text: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.
passages.sermon:
A crowd stood there.
The crowd heard a voice from heaven.
Some people in the crowd said it had thundered.
Other people said an angel had spoken to Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν ὄχλος ὁ ἑστὼς καὶ ἀκούσας ἔλεγεν Βροντὴν γεγονέναι ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Ἄγγελος αὐτῷ λελάληκεν

passages.text: In response, Jesus said, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He answered them.
He said, “This voice did not come for My sake.
This voice came for your sake.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Οὐ δι’ ἐμὲ ἡ φωνὴ αὕτη γέγονεν ἀλλὰ δι’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said that judgment has come to this world.\r\nHe said that the prince of this world will be cast out.
passages.original: νῦν κρίσις ἐστὶν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου νῦν ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἐκβληθήσεται ἔξω

passages.text: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus said, “When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw everyone to Myself.”
Jesus meant that He would die by being lifted up on a cross.
Jesus said He would bring all people to Himself through His death.
passages.original: κἀγὼ ἐὰν ὑψωθῶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς πάντας ἑλκύσω πρὸς ἐμαυτόν

passages.text: He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke these words.\r\nHe wanted to show what kind of death He would die.\r\nHe used these words to indicate His coming death.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνήσκειν

passages.text: The crowd replied, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
passages.sermon:
A crowd spoke to Jesus.
The crowd had heard the Law.
The Law said the Christ will remain forever.
The crowd asked Jesus a question.
They asked, “How can you say the Son of Man must be lifted up?”
They also asked, “Who is this Son of Man?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ πῶς λέγεις σὺ ὅτι δεῖ ὑψωθῆναι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Light.
Jesus said the Light will be with them for a little while longer.
He told them to walk while they have the Light.
He warned them so that darkness would not overtake them.
Anyone who walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔτι μικρὸν χρόνον τὸ φῶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν περιπατεῖτε ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε ἵνα μὴ σκοτία ὑμᾶς καταλάβῃ καὶ ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ οὐκ οἶδεν ποῦ ὑπάγει

passages.text: While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
Jesus called Himself the Light.
The Light was with the people for a little while.
Jesus told them to believe in the Light while they had it.
If they believed in the Light, they would become sons of light.
After Jesus said these things, He went away.
Jesus hid Himself from the people.
passages.original: ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε πιστεύετε εἰς τὸ φῶς ἵνα υἱοὶ φωτὸς γένησθε Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἐκρύβη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus performed many signs.
He did these signs in front of them.
They saw these signs.
They did not believe in Jesus.
passages.original: Τοσαῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ σημεῖα πεποιηκότος ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
God gave Isaiah a message.
God spoke through Isaiah.
God said, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
God also said, “To whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
These words from Isaiah needed to be fulfilled.
passages.original: ἵνα ὁ λόγος Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πληρωθῇ ὃν εἶπεν Κύριε τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν καὶ ὁ βραχίων Κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη

passages.text: For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.”
passages.sermon:
They could not believe.
This happened for a reason.
Isaiah spoke about this before.
Isaiah said, “God has blinded their eyes.”
He said, “God has hardened their hearts.”
They cannot see with their eyes.
They cannot understand with their hearts.
They cannot turn to God.
If they turned, God would heal them.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἠδύναντο πιστεύειν ὅτι πάλιν εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας Τετύφλωκεν αὐτῶν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ ἐπώρωσεν αὐτῶν τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα μὴ ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ νοήσωσιν τῇ καρδίᾳ καὶ στραφῶσιν καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς

passages.text: Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah saw Jesus’ glory.
Isaiah spoke about Jesus.
Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὅτι εἶδεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐλάλησεν περὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.
passages.sermon:
Many leaders believed in Jesus.
They did not confess their faith in Jesus.
They feared the Pharisees.
They did not want to be put out of the synagogue.
passages.original: ὅμως μέντοι καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς Φαρισαίους οὐχ ὡμολόγουν ἵνα μὴ ἀποσυνάγωγοι γένωνται

passages.text: For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.
passages.sermon:
Many leaders believed in Jesus.
They did not confess their faith because of the Pharisees.
They feared being put out of the synagogue.
These leaders loved praise from people.
They loved praise from people more than praise from God.
passages.original: ἠγάπησαν γὰρ τὴν δόξαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων μᾶλλον ἤπερ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Then Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke loudly.
Jesus said these words.
Anyone who believes in Me does not believe in Me alone.
Anyone who believes in Me also believes in the One who sent Me.
God sent Me.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἔκραξεν καὶ εἶπεν Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ πιστεύει εἰς ἐμὲ ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸν πέμψαντά με

passages.text: And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “Whoever sees Me also sees the One who sent Me.”
God sent Jesus.
If you look at Jesus, you are also looking at God who sent Him.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ θεωρῶν ἐμὲ θεωρεῖ τὸν πέμψαντά με

passages.text: I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus says, “I have come into the world.
I am a light.
I came so that everyone who believes in Me will not stay in darkness.”
passages.original: ἐγὼ φῶς εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐλήλυθα ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ μὴ μείνῃ

passages.text: As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the one sent by the Father.
If anyone hears the words of Jesus and does not keep them, Jesus does not judge that person.
Jesus did not come to judge the world.
Jesus came to save the world.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐάν τίς μου ἀκούσῃ τῶν ῥημάτων καὶ μὴ φυλάξῃ ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω αὐτόν οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον ἵνα κρίνω τὸν κόσμον ἀλλ’ ἵνα σώσω τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the one speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Anyone who rejects Jesus has a judge.
Anyone who does not receive the words of Jesus has a judge.
The word Jesus has spoken will judge that person.
This judgment will happen on the last day.
passages.original: ὁ ἀθετῶν ἐμὲ καὶ μὴ λαμβάνων τὰ ῥήματά μου ἔχει τὸν κρίνοντα αὐτόν ὁ λόγος ὃν ἐλάλησα ἐκεῖνος κρινεῖ αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus did not speak on His own authority.
The Father sent Jesus.
The Father gave Jesus a command.
The Father told Jesus what to say.
The Father told Jesus how to say it.
passages.original: Ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλάλησα ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με Πατὴρ αὐτός μοι ἐντολὴν δέδωκεν τί εἴπω καὶ τί λαλήσω

passages.text: And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus knows something important.
Jesus knows that the Father's command brings eternal life.
Jesus speaks only what the Father tells Him.
Jesus says everything just as the Father has said to Him.
passages.original: καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιός ἐστιν ἃ οὖν ἐγὼ λαλῶ καθὼς εἴρηκέν μοι ὁ Πατήρ οὕτως λαλῶ
